sources.label: Safirum press releases of June 22 and November 3 2026

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Issuer-documented transfer controls. Safirum's November 3 2026 launch release says every user must pass identity verification and that CHF-S can only be transferred between approved wallets. Its June 22 2026 release says wallet-level KYC whitelisting is embedded in the token's smart contract, and its website says only verified addresses can hold CHF-S, with the whitelist maintained on-chain by a four-party multi-signature system. Removing an address from that whitelist stops it from transacting, so the issuer side can block holders. The CHF-S mint address has not been published, so the whitelist authority and any freeze or permanent-delegate settings were not verified on-chain in this review.
